decisions.reason: A classic lever handle close to the core range in a growing market likely meets aspirations, and a large firm's slack makes carrying it cheap.
A handle family adds system breadth, which is central to the firm's strategy, and there is no sign of a shortfall that would trigger search.
A single new handle design within the established offer costs little to keep while industry turnover grows, though design lines are sometimes pruned.
A design handle near the core range with low incremental cost gives no reason to drop it while results appear satisfactory.
A handle family supports the integrated-system direction and is easy to carry with available slack.
The prominently launched L700 electronic access system fits the firm's push into digital building organization, so it will be carried even while results are uncertain.
